notes: This is a draft source register, not the completed 295-equation catalogue.
A source can support a family of equations but each entry must cite the exact page, section, theorem, or protocol version.
Do not treat algebraic rearrangements, unit conversions, parameter changes, or variable renamings as structurally distinct.
Protocol formulas must be version-tagged; Aave V3/V4 and Uniswap V2/V3/V4 mechanics are not interchangeable.
No calibration-ready independence claim is made by this manifest.
Consolidated bibliography and source metadata are maintained in docs/CORE295_REFERENCES.md; every accepted entry must still include its own exact source location and version.
Tumor-dynamics primary-source leads traced in discovery batch 3 are listed separately in the source register; they remain candidate references and do not approve or count any equation.

Primary biology source leads for Lotka population dynamics, Kermack–McKendrick epidemic theory, Turing morphogenesis and Gyenge physiological transport are recorded as candidate references only; none establishes an accepted equation or independent calibration unit.

Chemistry source-map expansion in discovery batch 4 adds mass-action historical provenance, IUPAC equilibrium/activity definitions, and OpenStax chapter coverage for equilibrium, acid-base, solubility, thermodynamics and electrochemistry; all remain candidate references.

Chemistry discovery batch 4 was deepened with primary/historical leads for Debye–Hückel electrolyte theory and van't Hoff temperature-dependent equilibrium, plus specific polyprotic-acid and conditional-solubility references; all are discovery-only candidate references.

OpenStax Chemistry 2e §11.3 provides a specific Henry's-law equation lead C_g = k P_g. This is a candidate gas–liquid solubility relation, not the excluded ideal-gas law; it remains a candidate reference pending benchmark suitability and source-family review.

Chemistry source mapping now includes surface adsorption (Langmuir 1918) and molecular diffusion (Fick 1855) as additional source-family leads; diffusion flux and diffusion PDE are related levels of one transport framework and must not be counted independently without an explicit sampling-unit rule.
